findings.claim: The split does not make the non-green representation total over its required failure inputs. Both event alternatives reused by bien_nhan_khong_xanh require a non-null run_created_at; schedule additionally requires khung_danh_nghia_utc derived from run.created_at. findings.claim: The consumer rules do not bind receipt rows bijectively to the independently expected/latest REST producers. C4 compares sets, C7 counts the submitted arrays, and C6 only compares attempts inside the receipt. Therefore a duplicate job with adjusted tally, a duplicate shard replacing another shard, a missing shard with 7/7, and stale attempt-1 producer rows under a run-attempt-2 receipt all satisfy the literal C1-C8 contract. Real archive/content hashes do not repair a missing relationship: authentic bytes can be duplicated, omitted or assigned to the wrong producer generation. X2/X4/X5 constrain the producer, but section 5 does not require consumers to recheck those relationships. An executor implementing exactly the advertised B2/B3 rules can accept incomplete or stale evidence.

There is no single collector YAML satisfying both rules, and the schema-over-prose rule cannot resolve a workflow-order contradiction.

findings.claim: Every one of the nine pattern sites accepts a trailing LF under the mandated jsonschema 4.26.0 validator. Dollar anchors match before a final newline. Thus sha40 accepts a 41-character string, digest accepts extra bytes, and timestamp/repository/positive-count patterns have the same defect. This contradicts the frozen exact lexical domains and creates parser-dependent shape acceptance for consumers. The checks are schema shape checks, so C1 cannot be relied on to reject these malformed spellings.
